What do you play when you just want to relax?
Forza Motorsport is my relaxing game. There's something about a good racing game that lulls you into that zen mode.

I've actually been considering getting back to forza since the xbox one race wheel has come down in price quite a bit. My only real complaint with racing games is I hate playing them with a gamepad or joystick.

I never liked the racing wheel, but my step-dad is also a Forza nut and he loves them. I got him one for Christmas last year - I think it's the Thrustmaster VG Ferrari 458 Spider Racing Wheel. It didn't come with a stand or anything to clamp it to, so he used a TV tray until he could build something out of wood. It ended up working quite well for him. I wish the wheels weren't so expensive - a racing wheel with force feedback and a proper mount is expensive - but as far as in-game support goes, Forza Motorsport 5 and 6 detected it and support it in their UIs just fine.

I actually have a Wheelstand Pro at home which I mount my thrustmaster warthog to. If he's looking for an alternative I can say the build quality is excellent, if a little pricey.

I agree about the force feedback wheel. I own a performance car IRL, and it makes a huge difference to feel somewhat "connected" to the road. It's probably why I can't get used to the idea of using a gamepad. Forza does a really amazing job of modeling car mechanics/physics. Mine is in Forza 5, and it's very close to what I would expect the car to do when actually driving.

Thanks for the tip :) he's pretty good with handiwork so he made something that suits him well, but I might keep that one in mind if I ever decide to jump in with a racing wheel full time. I love racing games, and I agree completely about Forza just nailing the physics of real driving, better than other racing games at least. It's probably the one platform exclusive I'd be sad to give up if I ever switched platforms, but I did hear something about Forza games coming out on PC in the future.
You and I approach racing games very differently. I love racing games, but the good ones are challenging and that sure as hell isn't "relaxing"!

Oh man, but that's the joy of it :) perfect turning circles and high speeds take a special kind of concentration where you just tune everything else out and stop thinking about the outside world.
